Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: The _____ was Geographical and historical region in Southeast Europe.
Thrace.fact: Thrace (, thrayss) is a geographical and historical region in Southeast Europe roughly corresponding to the province of Thrace in the Roman Empire. Bounded by the Balkan Mountains to the north, the Aegean Sea to the south, and the Black Sea to the east, it comprises present-day southeastern Bulgaria, northeastern Greece, and the European part of Turkey, corresponding to Northern, Western and East Thrace respectively.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: In classical antiquity, lands inhabited by ancient _____ extended also in the north to modern-day Northern Bulgaria and Romania and to the west into Northern Greece, North Macedonia and Serbia
Thrace.fact: In classical antiquity, lands inhabited by ancient Thracians extended also in the north to modern-day Northern Bulgaria and Romania and to the west into Northern Greece, North Macedonia and Serbia.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: The name Europe (ancient _____ṓpē Εὐρώπη), also at first referred to this region, before that term expanded to include its modern sense
Thrace.fact: The name Europe (ancient Greek Eurṓpē Εὐρώπη), also at first referred to this region, before that term expanded to include its modern sense.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: In one ancient Greek source, the very Earth is divided into "Asia, Libya, Europa and _____"
Thrace.fact: The ancient Greeks employed the term "Thrace" to refer to all of the territory which lay north of Thessaly inhabited by the Thracians, a region which "had no definite boundaries" and to which other regions (like Macedonia and even Scythia) were added. In one ancient Greek source, the very Earth is divided into "Asia, Libya, Europa and Thracia".

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: This largely coincided with the _____ kingdom, whose borders varied over time
Thrace.fact: This largely coincided with the Thracian Odrysian kingdom, whose borders varied over time.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society

Thrace.fact: After the Macedonian conquest, this region's former border with ancient Macedonia was shifted from the Struma River to the Mesta River.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: This usage lasted until the _____ conquest
Thrace.fact: This usage lasted until the Roman conquest. In its early period, the Roman province of Thrace was of this extent, but after the administrative reforms of the late 3rd century, Thracia's much reduced territory became the six small provinces which constituted the Diocese of Thrace.

Thrace.fact: In Summer 1934, up to 10,000 Jews were maltreated, bereaved, and then forced to quit the region (see 1934 Thrace pogroms). From Bulgaria and Romania between 1934 and 1938 a large wave of Muslim immigrants went to East Thrace.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society

Thrace.subject: Indian Society

Thrace.fact: Cisseus, father-in-law to the Trojan elder Antenor, is also given as a Thracian king.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: Greek mythology is replete with _____ kings, including Diomedes, Tereus, Lycurgus, Phineus, Tegyrius, Eumolpus, Polymnestor, Poltys, and Oeagrus (father of Orpheus)
Thrace.fact: The Catalogue of Ships mentions three separate contingents from Thrace: Thracians led by Acamas and Peiros, from Aenus; Cicones led by Euphemus, from southern Thrace, near Ismaros; and from the city of Sestus, on the Thracian (northern) side of the Hellespont, which formed part of the contingent led by Asius. Ancient Thrace was home to numerous other tribes, such as the Edones, Bisaltae, Cicones, and Bistones in addition to the tribe that Homer specifically calls the "Thracians".

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: She and her sister, _____, plot to get revenge, by killing her son Itys (by Tereus) and serving him to his father for dinner
Thrace.fact: Thrace is mentioned in Ovid's Metamorphoses, in the episode of Philomela, Procne, and Tereus: Tereus, the King of Thrace, lusts after his sister-in-law, Philomela. She and her sister, Procne, plot to get revenge, by killing her son Itys (by Tereus) and serving him to his father for dinner.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
Thrace.question: At the end of the myth, all three turn into birds – Procne into a swallow, _____ into a nightingale, and Tereus into a hoopoe
Thrace.fact: Philomela manages to get free, however. At the end of the myth, all three turn into birds – Procne into a swallow, Philomela into a nightingale, and Tereus into a hoopoe.

Thrace.subject: Indian Society

Thrace.subject: Indian Society
